hook: A U.S. military electro-optical or infrared sensor captured two anomalous objects — one structured with an appendage, one smaller and circular — in a monochrome still image submitted by the FBI to AARO in 2025, with the original imagery redacted prior to submission.
why_it_matters: This submission represents a rare instance of the FBI formally channeling military sensor imagery to AARO under the post-NDAA UAP reporting framework, demonstrating inter-agency UAP data sharing in practice. The operator's inability to positively identify the objects, combined with the absence of an accompanying mission report, leaves the sighting unresolved and limits analytical follow-up. The image's corrupted timestamp — caused by an unconfigured system clock — illustrates a recurring data-integrity problem that complicates UAP event reconstruction.

key_findings.finding: The image contains two spatially distinct anomalous objects: a dark, structured object with a left-side appendage near the crosshair reticle, and a smaller dark circular object in the lower-right quadrant.
The original military sensor imagery was altered through redactions before being forwarded to AARO, meaning the submitted image does not represent the full unmodified capture.
No mission report accompanied the image submission, stripping it of operational context such as altitude, speed, sensor mode, or crew observations.
The image's embedded date/time is incorrect because the originating system's clock was never properly configured, undermining chronological anchoring of the event.
The reporting operator could not positively identify either object, satisfying the threshold for formal UAP submission under current DoD/IC reporting policy.

legacy_program_connections.reasoning: AARO is the direct recipient of this FBI-submitted military sensor image, representing the formal UAP reporting pipeline established under post-NDAA disclosure requirements.
The image originates from an unspecified U.S. military sensor system, which may fall under Air Force materiel and intelligence collection infrastructure historically centered at Wright-Patterson.
The unidentified military sensor platform that captured the imagery could involve reconnaissance or surveillance systems within the NRO's domain, though no direct connection is stated.
